study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized functional connectome abnormalities obtained using two normative model unveil neurophysiological subtypes of obsessive compulsive disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Single-site cohort: 99 patients with OCD and 104 healthy controls; patients recruited at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University and HCs recruited from the community.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We recruited a total of 99 patients with OCD and 104 healthy controls (HCs) matched for demographic characteristics."; "...recruited from outpatient services within the Department of Psychiatry at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University."; "Healthy controls (HCs, n = 104) were enlisted from the community via poster advertisements."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Liu2024.pdf.md: Abstract, Paragraph 1; Methods / Participants, Paragraph 1; Methods / Participants, Paragraph 2

answer.SINGLE-SITE: HCs used to train/validate the normative model of FCS; OCD patients used for application of the normative model and subtype discovery

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Gaussian process regression normative model trained within HCs (10-fold cross-validation) and applied to OCD patients to derive individualized FCS abnormalities used for clustering.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "First, we evaluated the performance of the Gaussian process regression model in predicting FCS values within HCs through 10-fold crossvalidation... Subsequently, for each brain region, a Gaussian process regression model was trained to estimate the normative range of FCS values as a function of age and sex within HCs. This model was then applied to each patient, yielding a predicted FCS value."; "We recruited a total of 99 patients with OCD and 104 healthy controls (HCs)"
